expression_comparison.chosen_because: USDJPY has already sold off ~4% over 3m and sits only around the 30th 1y percentile, so USD spot is a noisier hawk expression than paying UST 2Y.

considered_rates.assessment: US 10Y 4.94 is near the 1y 97.8th percentile with a 45.000000000000014bp 3m change; AU 2Y 4.835 sits at the 99.8th 1y percentile while Australian housing is tightening.
US 2s10s is 27.000000000000046bp at the 1.4th 1y percentile, so curve is an executable alternative to spot or outright duration.
CA-US 5Y is -122.00000000000001bp at the 0.2th 1y percentile — a historically extreme cross-market RV object.

considered_spot.assessment: USDJPY is available but the 3m decline and mid-low percentile make it a worse policy-path instrument than front-end duration.

remit: currencies where inflation and policy risks are underpriced to the upside
stance_summary: Inflation persistence after the first Warsh hike is cleaner as short UST 2Y than as USDJPY.

evidence_refs: rollup:August CPI keeps the Fed tightening bias intact
rollup:BoC minutes flag higher energy pass-through risk
trade.invalidation: A Fed communication that closes further hikes or a documented US labor/activity break.
trade.mispricing: The delivered 25bp hike is being treated as a completed cycle while US 2Y is already at the 99th 1y percentile because the path, not the first move, is the object.
principal_risks: The 99th-percentile 2Y is already the hawkish view
trade.thesis: Energy, import prices, Michigan inflation expectations and Warsh's inflation emphasis keep additional US restraint underpriced.
why_now: FOMC hike plus energy and import-price evidence remain inside the cutoff.
